title: Msafe Equipments Ltd - 544695 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Msafe FY26 revenue rose about 45% to Rs 103.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 39.49% and PAT at Rs 22.02 crore (+72%).
summary.overview: Management's first earnings call after IPO reported FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 103.5 crore (up ~45% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 49.9 crore (up ~57%) and PAT of Rs 22.02 crore (up ~72%). EBITDA margin widened to 39.49% from 36.55%, driven by the rental mix and utilisation. Management said MS scaffolding capacity has reached about 6,285 tonnes via temporary rented-premise facilities, ahead of IPO timelines, and entered aluminium formwork. Guidance calls for ~50% CAGR, with the mix shifting toward lower-margin sales, rising capex (~Rs 130 crore) and rising debt.

financial_highlights.change: Rental share fell from 63% over the last few years

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 5 crore total (~Rs 2.5 crore sales, ~Rs 2.5 crore rental)

financial_highlights.change: Increased as yards went from 4 to 18

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 4-5 crore, debt-free (per analyst's figure); analyst also cited ~Rs 38 crore on books

segments.name: Steel (MS) scaffolding
segments.commentary: FY26 total sales plus rental only ~Rs 5 crore. Management guided FY27 to Rs 25-40 crore (5-10x), with steel sales gross margin of ~5-6% and rental yield of 32-38% p.a. Current run-rate cited as ~Rs 1 crore/month rental and ~Rs 1 crore/month sales.

segments.name: Aluminium scaffolding
segments.commentary: ~Rs 98 crore in FY26, roughly split 50-50 sales and rental; current run-rate cited as ~Rs 3 crore/month sales and ~Rs 3.5 crore/month rental. Rental yield 60-66% p.a.; sales gross margin ~30%. Targeted growth ~20% in FY27 core business.

segments.name: Aluminium formwork (new)
segments.commentary: Flagship product launched in FY26; machinery ordered, production targeted by end-June 2026. First-year target Rs 30-40 crore; gross margin guided at ~10% initially, ~15% long term. Management expects at least 30% of revenue from rental.

segments.name: Industrial ladders / safety products
segments.commentary: Ladder manufacturing started, with a proposed channel partner model (none currently). Trading of industrial safety products deferred 3-4 months; no manufacturing planned for those.

guidance_outlook: Management says it expects ~50% CAGR, and later cited a 50-70% CAGR aim; it confirmed FY27 revenue of 'definitely' above Rs 150 crore is achievable but declined to commit to a PAT figure.
Core business growth ~20% in FY27; steel scaffolding growing multiple-fold; formwork a new division with a modest target.
FY27 revenue mix expected around 40% rental and 60% sales; sales share may rise to 60-40 or 38-72 range.
EBITDA margin may fluctuate and drift lower from ~40% as sales mix rises, but management aims to maintain the range and offset via topline.
Total capex ~Rs 130 crore in FY27 including rental assets and new plant; funding via debt plus earnings, with expected PAT of Rs 30-40 crore this year.
Partial aluminium capacity addition from December 2026, full completion by May 2027; owned factory commissioning expected by May 2027.
capex_capacity: MS scaffolding capacity doubled to ~6,285 tonnes (cited as 62.85 lakh units) via temporary facilities on rented premises; running near full utilisation, sometimes 24 hours.
Aluminium scaffolding: plan to add ~10 lakh units; a few ladder machines added; full addition tied to new factory, partial start by December 2026, complete by May 2027.
Owned MS facility expected to commence by May 2027; temporary capacity to be reviewed then.
Warehouses (yards) grew from 4 to 18; plan to add 4-5 yards a year (Surat/Bharuch, Cochin/Trivandrum, Goa) and cut reach from 500 km to 250 km radius.
IPO proceeds: ~25% used for rental assets by FY26 (rest by 2H FY27); ~11% used for manufacturing and rental expansion, with land acquisition advanced and advanced machines ordered.
demand_pricing: Operating at ~1,000-1,500 sites with ~2,500 customers; pan-India presence versus mostly regional peers; ~20 years of operating experience.
Sales are short-cycle (orders up to 7 days), so aluminium price changes are passed on; rental rates are sticky, so the company absorbs some cost increases.
Aluminium prices reportedly up 40-50%; the company holds large inventory, with a 30% year-end price increase cited, so benefit is not yet fully on the books.
Bad debts under 2% over six years; new customers pay 1-3 months' rental as advance.
Competition: management says there are no entry barriers, with Technocraft cited as a possible entrant in rental and formwork.

qa_highlights.question: Is steel capacity at peak utilisation, and what is the revenue from it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the factory is fully occupied, running around the clock. Steel generates ~Rs 1 crore/month rental and ~Rs 1 crore/month sales, with ~70% of material on rent and 25-30% sold.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~40% EBITDA and ~22% PAT margins sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the mix to change as formwork (mostly sales) and steel grow. The 40% margin may fluctuate slightly, but the company aims to hold the range.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and EBITDA evolve with lower-margin segments growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EBITDA percentage may decline but absolute impact is minimal, and topline growth will offset this. It said its internal targets are much higher than guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex and debt be funded in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex ~Rs 130 crore; funding through debt plus internal accruals, with expected PAT of Rs 30-40 crore. Debt will rise and is typically repaid within 3 years, though debt may be lower if accruals suffice.

qa_highlights.question: Why do customers rent at 32-66% yields rather than buy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited project-based needs, multi-site logistics, capital constraints, and scaffolding being under 1% of project cost. Yields reflect short economic life (aluminium ~5 years vs steel 10-15), with scrap value recoverable.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up to ~Rs 24 crore and ~80 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose from yard expansion (4 to 18), a 30% year-end metal price rise, and precautionary stock; management expects normalisation over time.

risks_watch: Margin dilution as low-margin steel and formwork sales grow; steel sales gross margin only ~5-6%.
Capex of ~Rs 130 crore with rising debt; net cash position reverses to net debt; interest and depreciation increase.
Execution risk on the new formwork plant (production targeted end-June 2026) and on aluminium factory timelines (December 2026 to May 2027).
Competitive entry in rental (e.g., Technocraft) could compress the 32-66% yields that drive profitability.
Aluminium and steel price volatility, rental rate stickiness and inventory valuation; ~Rs 2.87 crore loss on scrapped or lost assets, which management says is recurring.
Factory-level attrition above 50%, per the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and yields, with repeated assurances that margins and the 50% CAGR will be met. Evasive on specifics: declined to give PAT or margin guidance for FY27, and gave only approximate figures on capacity revenue, citing compliance limits.
key_quotes: We will definitely achieve a 50% CAGR because our vision is much more than that.
We won't let you down on the bottom line.
Currently, my factory is working throughout the day, sometimes 24 hours, and we are fully jam-packed.

Aluminium formwork production line, machinery ordered, production targeted end-June 2026 (first-year target Rs 30-40 cr)
Owned MS scaffolding factory, commissioning by May 2027

growth.why: Management guides ~50% revenue CAGR and FY27 revenue above Rs 150 crore (core ~20% growth, steel Rs 25-40 cr, formwork Rs 30-40 cr), backed by utilisation at ~100%, a 10 lakh-unit aluminium addition (partial Dec 2026, full May 2027) and an owned MS factory by May 2027, but no firm order book was cited and capex of ~Rs 130 cr is funded partly by debt.
